why: Quote verified verbatim at errors.md:1400 (whole line read; no reversing second sentence). But the finding cites the WRONG LAYER, and its three-part description of our state is false at the layer that actually does the work. (1) The cited code, spawner.ts:296-298 `allowedTools()`, filters the declared list against `disallowedTools` only -- exactly as claimed -- yet errors.md:1406 explicitly carves that case OUT of the refusal: 'Omitting the `tools` field never triggers this refusal. If you leave the `tools` list empty, or `disallowedTools` removes every entry in it, Claude Code also skips the refusal and launches the subagent without tools.' So the one line cited as evidence is conformant, not divergent. (2) The layer that handles the doc's three groups is upstream: `resolveExplicitTools` / `buildPiRuntimeAgentDefinitions` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/runtime-agent-definitions.ts:92-126 and :129-179), called in production at packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1313 with the session's real tool set (`manifest.tools.map(t => t.binding.piName)` plus `manifest.deferredMcp.candidatePiNames`). It resolves each declared name exactly, case-insensitively, then via PI_RUNTIME_AGENT_TOOL_ALIASES. 'Unrecognized' -> pushed onto `unresolved` and `throw new Error('Unavailable runtime agent tool(s): ...')` at :122-124 (fail-closed, and STRICTER than Claude, which refuses only when ALL entries fail). 'Not available to subagents' -> SUBAGENT_UNAVAILABLE_TOOLS (:50) stripped at :125, and ORCHESTRATION_TOOLS (:33-40) withheld from a tool-less descriptor's ceiling. 'Matched no tools in this session' -> a recognized alias with no counterpart in this manifest is 'denied by omission' at :116-120. The host re-validates the arriving list against the pinned definition (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:10859, `runtime-agent-tool-unavailable:<tool>`) and re-filters it against `parentTools` at :10994. So 'unrecognised names, names not available to subagents, and names matching nothing in the session are all passed through unvalidated' is wrong on all three counts -- the textbook 'identifier unwired but consequence false because something upstream already handled it'. (3) Only a narrow residual survives: there is no 'Agent would be spawned with zero tools - refusing' refusal with entries grouped by cause (`grep -a` for 'zero tools'/'resolved to nothing' over all TS sources returns only an unrelated MCP test). A list whose entries all resolve to dropped entries yields `effectiveTools` = union with SUBAGENT_ALWAYS_AVAILABLE_TOOLS (runtime-agent-definitions.ts:83, :149) -- usually five task/report tools, occasionally empty -- and the spawn proceeds. That is Claude's own pre-v2.1.208 behaviour (errors.md:1408), and it is a missing diagnostic, not the unvalidated pass-through the finding describes. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3, and not a branding/product difference.
correctedState: Declared subagent `tools` entries ARE validated, one layer above the cited line. `resolveExplicitTools` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/runtime-agent-definitions.ts:92-126), reached in production from index.ts:1313 with the session's actual Pi manifest tool names, throws `Unavailable runtime agent tool(s): <name>` on an unrecognised entry (:122-124), strips SUBAGENT_UNAVAILABLE_TOOLS (:50, :125), and denies a recognised alias with no counterpart in this session by omission (:116-120); SessionManager.ts:10859 and :10994 re-validate and re-filter host-side. `allowedTools()` at spawner.ts:296-298 applies only the `disallowedTools` subtraction, which errors.md:1406 explicitly exempts from the refusal. The genuine, much smaller gap is that we have no equivalent of the v2.1.208 'Agent would be spawned with zero tools - refusing' guard: when every entry drops out, the child launches with only SUBAGENT_ALWAYS_AVAILABLE_TOOLS (possibly none) and no grouped diagnostic naming which entries failed and why.
